item.title: A new way of doing business: From Business Innovation to Social Change
item.content:encoded:
Ricardo Costa-Climent, University of Valencia

Steve D'Alessandro, Edith Cowan University

By centring mechanisms (identity, norms, trust/fairness, agency, and risk–value trade-offs), this special issue aims to explain when and why new ways of doing business achieve social impact through consumer behaviour, and how organisations can design enduring, equitable, and scalable change.

Potential topics

  • Identity mechanisms in business innovation
  • Norms and their role in social change
  • Trust and fairness in organizational design
  • Agency in consumer behavior and social impact
  • Risk-value trade-offs in business models
  • Consumer behavior and social impact achievement
  • Design of enduring and equitable organizational change
  • Scalable business models for social change

Timeline

  • February 15, 2026: Submission window opens
  • September 15, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Emotion by Design: The Emotional Architecture of Consumer Behaviour in an Era of Emerging Technologies
item.content:encoded:
Aude Rychalski, ESSCA School of Management

Varsha Jain, ESSCA School of Management

Elodie Jouny-Rivier, ESSCA School of Management

Anupama Ambika, IMT

This Special Issue invites interdisciplinary contributions exploring how emerging technologies like AI, AR, VR, XR, and others dynamically shape consumer emotions, eventually influencing identity and behaviour. The issue welcomes theoretical, empirical, and methodological paper submissions from consumer behaviour, consumer psychology, human technology interaction, digital media, and related areas.

The focus is on exploring the mechanisms, processes, and consequences in the context of technology-enabled emotion engineering. Additionally, discussions are encouraged on consumer autonomy, well-being, and broader implications of emotionally engineered consumer behaviour.

Potential topics

  • How emerging technologies (AI, AR, VR, XR, and others) shape consumer emotions
  • Influence of technology-induced emotions on consumer identity and behaviour
  • Mechanisms and processes of technology-enabled emotion engineering
  • Consequences of emotionally engineered consumer behaviour
  • Consumer autonomy in the context of emotional technology design
  • Consumer well-being implications of emotion engineering
  • Broader societal implications of emotionally engineered consumer behaviour

Timeline

  • November 1, 2026: Submissions window opens
  • December 30, 2026: Submissions window closes

item.title: Consumer Vulnerability in the Age of Algorithmic Persuasion: Risks, Responsibilities, and Remedies
item.content:encoded:
Jenny Le, VinUniversity

Helen Chun, Cornell University

Sara Quach, Griffith University

Park Thaichon, University of Southern Queensland

This Special Issue aims to advance ethics of algorithmic persuasion in marketing. It seeks to fill the critical gaps related to the underexplored mechanisms by which AI technologies construct, amplify, or mitigate consumer vulnerability; the limited empirical evidence on how privacy risks intersect with persuasion strategies; and the insufficient integration of ethical principles into the design of AI-powered marketing systems.

Potential topics

  • Mechanisms by which AI technologies construct, amplify, or mitigate consumer vulnerability
  • Privacy risks and their intersection with persuasion strategies
  • Ethical principles in the design of AI-powered marketing systems
  • Ethics of algorithmic persuasion in marketing

Timeline

  • July 1, 2027: Submission window opens
  • August 30, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Influence of Agentic AI in Consumer Behaviour: Future Landscape
item.content:encoded:
Rahul Sindhwani, Indian Institute of Management – Sambalpur

Varsha Jain, ESSCA School of Management

Justin Zhang, University of North Florida

Sudhir Rana, Liwa University

This Special Issue aims to advance both theory and practice regarding consumer behavior in the age of agentic AI. Theoretically, it seeks to deepen understanding of how autonomous AI agents influence fundamental consumer processes such as decision-making, trust, perceived autonomy, and engagement.

Potential topics

  • Consumer decision-making with autonomous AI agents
  • Trust in agentic AI systems
  • Perceived autonomy in AI-influenced consumer processes
  • Consumer engagement with autonomous AI agents
  • Theoretical frameworks for agentic AI and consumer behavior
  • Practical applications of agentic AI in consumer markets
  • Autonomous agents and fundamental consumer processes

Timeline

  • July 1, 2027: Submission window opens
  • December 31, 2027: Submission window closes
